summary: Evening burst causes dedicated pool throughput sag and elevated tail latency (suspected noisy tenant + autoscale undersizing)
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-09 18:10-19:05 UTC we observed a sustained degradation in throughput and a sharp rise in p95/p99 for GlideAI's dedicated reservation in us-west. Symptoms started after an evening traffic spike. Impact: production endpoints returned 504/stream timeouts and request throughput fell ~45% compared to baseline, causing customer LLM features to fail for end users. Environment: Dedicated GPU reservation (resv-glas-13b), single pool in prod-us-west serving mixed model variants. Observed at ~18:10 UTC when a tenant in the same pool exhibited a high burst of long-sequence requests.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate 60-90s burst from a single tenant with interleaved long context (seq_len ~2048) and high token generation rate; 2) Run concurrent steady traffic from GlideAI baseline workload (shorter sequences, high qps); 3) Monitor serving runtime queue length, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and scheduler pending queue; 4) Observe tail latency elevation and 5xx/timeouts on baseline requests.
logs_excerpt:
[2026-03-09T18:12:04Z] WARNING serving-runtime: queue_depth=312 gpu_util=87% pending_evictions=6
[2026-03-09T18:12:06Z] ERROR scheduler: request_timeout for job_id=glide-req-88923 status=504
[2026-03-09T18:13:10Z] INFO autoscaler: scale_event=blocked reason=insufficient_gpu_slots current_replicas=4 max_replicas=4
[2026-03-09T18:14:30Z] WARN kernel: gpu_mem_pressure=true vram_paging=3 BPF=low
metrics_snapshot: At 18:12 UTC: p50=120ms p95=1.6s p99=4.8s error_rate=12% throughput=220rps (baseline 400rps). GPU utilization per-card: 92%, 91%, 88%, 25% (one card lower due to job packing imbalance). Scheduler pending queue length peaked at 320. KV cache hit ratio dropped from 78% to 33% for mixed-tenant traffic.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-09 18:20: initial triage — metrics show sustained high queue depth and uneven GPU utilization; eviction logs present but not excessive.
Hypothesis A: Noisy tenant submitted long-seq jobs that consumed large KV cache and pinned kernels, reducing throughput for others.
Hypothesis B: Autoscaler configured with conservative max_replicas=4 for this reservation; during burst, scheduler could not provision additional replicas leading to queue build-up.
Checked: kube events for GPU preemption and node autoscaling — no node-level scaling actions recorded; cluster had available nodes but pool-level quota prevented new replica placement.
Ran targeted repro in staging with synthetic burst — reproduced p95 elevation and observed job packing into same GPU causing head-of-line blocking.
Correlation: affected_models include a 13B variant that performs poorly with long context in current kernel selection, amplifying per-request GPU time.

Temporary mitigation applied at 18:45 UTC: migrated the noisy tenant's jobs off the shared pool and bumped max_replicas to 6 for the reservation. Observed throughput recovery to ~360rps over 12 minutes.
Follow-up: need autoscale policy review and tenant isolation strategies to prevent cross-tenant tail impact.
customer_communication: 2026-03-09 18:25 UTC — Support to customer: We've detected elevated latencies and are investigating. Please provide any traffic changes on your side.
2026-03-09 18:33 UTC — Customer (GlideAI): Confirmed a scheduled model sweep causing heavy long-context traffic starting ~18:05 UTC. Impacting their UI features.

2026-03-09 19:05 UTC — Support to customer: Migrated noisy workload to a temporary isolated pool and adjusted autoscale; monitoring for stabilization. Suggested follow-up actions included pacing and model pinning for long-context jobs.
resolution: Applied immediate mitigations: 1) Isolated noisy tenant by creating a temporary dedicated pool and routing their traffic there; 2) Increased reservation max_replicas from 4 to 6 to allow additional parallelism; 3) Adjusted scheduler packing policy to avoid tight co-location of long-seq jobs with high-qps tenants. Post-change metrics returned to ~90% of baseline throughput and error rate fell below 1% within 15 minutes.
follow_up_tasks: Adjust autoscale policy for resv-glas-13b: raise max_replicas and add a burst-mode with faster scale-up sensitive to queue depth.
Implement tenant burst isolation flag to automatically route large long-sequence jobs to separate pools when detected.
Add a targeted alert: sustained queue_depth > 200 for >3 minutes for dedicated pools (pager to on-call SRE).
Benchmark long-context kernel paths for affected 13B model variants and add optimized kernel profile or recommend quantization/sequence-splitting to customers.
Document recommended customer-side mitigations (rate-limiting long-seq sweeps, sandboxing experiments) and share with GlideAI.
Create post-incident runbook entry and link to related confluence page.
